title: MNS Suporte Implementation Plan
html:
Product scope · Human actions · Validation

MNS Suporte was initialized from Orion on 2026-11-25. The manifest records its foundation ancestry.

Tracking

The V1 denominator is the number of rows in V1 work. Count a row as complete only after its acceptance criteria pass with recorded evidence. Report completed, in-progress, pending, and blocked counts on each handoff. Project decisions stay in the product scope or relevant ADR. Access that requires a human stays in the human-action checklist. Preserve task IDs and record scope changes here.

V1 work

Task Deliverable and acceptance Status Evidence or dependency
PJ-01 Establish the GitHub repository with the owner-approved visibility. Verify the default branch, vulnerability alerts and enforced CI gate. completed The owner made the repository public. The default branch is main and vulnerability alerts are enabled. The active ruleset requires pull requests with the GitHub Actions Orion required gate check passing on an up-to-date branch and blocks force pushes and deletion. The latest CI on main passed.
PJ-02 Record actors, scope, data ownership, first-release acceptance and the future AI boundary. completed Approved scope and acceptance.
PJ-06 Implement Meta callback verification and signed webhook ingestion. Verify the challenge, exact-byte HMAC, incoming identity fields and recipient scope with synthetic requests. completed Webhook tests passed. The API guide documents configuration.
PJ-07 Persist incoming messages before acknowledgement and deduplicate replays, including concurrent delivery, using the restricted database role. completed Webhook integration tests verified concurrent replays, PostgreSQL grants and failure acknowledgement.
PJ-08 Implement the Meta outbound adapter and durable sends. Test text and interactive replies, safe retries and delivery status handling. completed Adapter, outbox and delivery, and worker lifecycle verified with a synthetic Meta transport and migrated PostgreSQL. Live pilot remains under PJ-17.
PJ-09 Implement the GLPI adapter and exact directory lookup. Test scoped credentials, timeouts, session renewal and explicit outcomes for mutations. completed Seven contract and transport tests passed. Company GLPI testing remains under PH-08 and PJ-17.
PJ-10 Verify and persist employee identity with short-lived, rate-limited email challenges. Test invalid, replayed and expired codes, and access isolation between employees. completed Identity integration and SMTP TLS checks passed. PJ-11 connects these operations to the signed conversation. The live relay remains under PH-09 and PJ-17.
PJ-11 Implement the menu, guided intake, resumable drafts, confirmation, editing and cancellation. Test ordinary navigation and restart recovery. completed Signed conversation integration covers runtime wiring, code recovery, draft restart, stale review buttons and sender isolation. Intake collects the employee's title and description, with optional media at review. Existing drafts preserve their description and media. The signed integration verifies the menu and GLPI payload. Submission and listing remain under PJ-13 and PJ-14.
PJ-12 Provide approved static troubleshooting with a direct path to open a ticket. Record whether it helped. completed Guidance tests cover selection, resolution and bypass. The conversation integration verifies restart and durable feedback for signed input.
PJ-13 Create GLPI tickets with attachments and confirmed summaries. Test duplicates, ambiguous creation outcomes and recoverable attachment failures. completed Signed conversation integration covers confirmed fields and media upload with provider fixtures. Worker recovery tests cover concurrent claims, ambiguous creation and attachment recovery. Live acceptance remains under PJ-17.
PJ-14 List the employee's open GLPI tickets and show authorized ticket details. Test ownership before disclosure and preserve existing ticket access through verified identity. completed GLPI contract tests cover scoped paging and actor roles. Signed conversation tests cover legacy tickets, unauthorized lookups and binding changes. Dispatch tests exercise reauthorization on retry. Live acceptance remains under PJ-17.
PJ-15 Notify on public support replies, observed status changes and closure with the current solution. Capture consent at confirmation and honor opt-out. Verify retries and delivery tracking. completed Closure lifecycle tests cover public replies, status, one formatted closure with the current solution, opt-out, GLPI retries and delivery status. Graph fixtures cover the approved-template payload and service-window behavior. Live Meta approval and use remain under PH-07 and PJ-17.
PJ-16 Package and document operation with a container, production configuration, restricted database access, retention, backup and restore, sanitized diagnostics, alerts and recovery procedures. Verify local deployment and rollback rehearsal. completed The disposable Compose rehearsal verified startup, restricted roles, retention and alerts, encrypted backup, corruption and duplicate rejection, fresh restore and rollback to the previous Git image with data intact. The runbook covers hosting and cutover. Company access remains under PH-10.
PJ-19 Triage GitHub dependency alerts and upgrade affected dependencies or document verified non-applicability. Revalidate the lockfile and runtime boundaries before the pilot. completed All eight baseline alerts were addressed. pnpm audit and pnpm audit --prod reported zero known findings. The API uses patched minimatch, the migration toolchain uses patched Effect, the web build uses patched Seroval, and the test toolchain uses patched glob. The Compose rehearsal checks that Prisma CLI and Effect stay out of the API image. Dependabot alerts.
PJ-17 Run the release acceptance suite against disposable infrastructure, then run a pilot with the test Meta number, authorized GLPI instance and mail relay. Verify real delivery and draft recovery. completed The signed conversation suite passed with synthetic providers. In the authorized local pilot, Meta verified the restricted HTTPS callback and delivered messages. The pilot verified corporate mailbox onboarding, requester isolation, synthetic ticket creation and attachment recovery, WhatsApp ticket consultation, and closure delivery within the customer service window. A worker restart recovered a guided draft, and a workstation restart preserved verified identities, consent, and delivery history.
PJ-20 Support independently verified WhatsApp accounts for one GLPI user. Give authorized IT staff a masked list and per-link revocation. completed Identity integration verifies two WhatsApp accounts, scoped access and revocation. PH-12 tracks operator access for the company deployment.
PJ-18 Reconcile active legacy notifications and onboard verified employees. Deploy, verify smoke checks and supervise the switch to the corporate support number. in progress The pilot is complete. Release preparation starts by validating and integrating the pilot changes into the protected default branch. Company hosting and the support number remain under PH-07 and PH-10.

Plan changes and later work

  • Meta verified the replacement local pilot callback for PJ-20 and retained the pilot account subscription and messages field. The previous test identity expired locally. The second WhatsApp account completed corporate email onboarding, linked to the same GLPI user, and read the menu. The first account can link again through the same flow.
  • PJ-20 recognizes a signed number already listed uniquely in the active GLPI directory after the corresponding email is entered. The adapter and signed conversation tests verified the direct menu, code fallback and revocation behavior. A read-only check against the company directory matched the existing email and detected that the pilot phone is listed on two active users, so it remains on the email-code path.
  • PJ-03 was the generic first module. PJ-06 through PJ-15 replace it with independently verifiable product capabilities.
  • PJ-04 remains outside V1. The web shell already provides the local documentation portal and is available for a future operator interface.
  • PJ-05 is split across PJ-10 and PJ-16. Corporate email verification is the V1 identity mechanism, with deployment work verified independently.
  • Post-V1 candidates include supplementing tickets over WhatsApp, known incident notices, an editorial knowledge base, and optional AI guidance and summarization. The AI extension boundary governs that work. These items are outside the V1 progress denominator.
